key_provisions_or_claims: 90.8% of respondents support a dedicated federal law on robotics.
84.1% consider existing robotics regulation gaps or insufficient.
87.9% support criminal liability for violating robot rules causing dangerous consequences, many depending on consequences.
86.5% favour separate criminal offence for arming robots; 68.3% see armed autonomous robots as threat to humanity.
73.6% think existing legal mechanisms cannot assess harm by autonomous robots absent a guilty person; 93.5% want criminal law amendments.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article reporting a 2021 online survey of 305 Russian legal professionals on criminal-law regulation of robotics. Findings show strong support for a dedicated federal robotics law, criminal liability for dangerous robot misuse, criminalising armed and crime-designed robots, and new mechanisms for harm by autonomous robots without a culpable human.
annotation.title_clean: Criminal Law Regulation of Robotics: Results of a Sociological Study
